note: Authoritative flash/clock parameters for the two X-Plus 4 MCUs. Every value is DERIVED (never copied from a QIDI binary); 'evidence' says how. A board whose status is 'unresolved' is never built into a release bundle (mcu/build-mcu.sh gate) and never written by eitri-mcuflash (installer/mcuflash boards.json carries the same status). Keep this file and installer/mcuflash/eitri_mcuflash/boards.json in step; mcu/tests/test_params.py fails when they drift.

mainboard.bootloader: Stock QIDI/Makerbase bootloader at 0x08000000, about 32 KiB. Not Katapult. Two entry paths: a UART protocol (hid-flash, 115200 8N1) and the SD-card path (qd_mcu.bin to qd_mcu.CUR). Never deploy Katapult here: that overwrites the bootloader.
mainboard.bootloader_baud: 115200 8N1 for the hid-flash UART path (the application runs at 500000); not applicable to the SD path
mainboard.method: Application-only write, bootloader preserved. Preferred: Klipper scripts/flash-sdcard.sh -b 500000 /dev/ttyS0 qidi-plus4 (needs a running Klipper application and a FAT32 card in the slot). Fallback: copy the image as qd_mcu.bin to the SD card and power-cycle. The pinned Kalico has no qidi-plus4 board definition, so Kalico trees use the card fallback or the pinned Klipper script tree.
evidence: Live klippy.log of the printer: MCU=stm32f401xc CLOCK_FREQ=84000000 RESERVE_PINS_crystal=PH0,PH1 RESERVE_PINS_serial=PA10,PA9 SERIAL_BAUD=500000 (an external crystal is present; its frequency is not printed).

Offset: a community Plus 4 mainboard Klipper image (not QIDI-authored) has its reset handler code at the position that is consistent only with a link address of 0x08008000, and boots on this board family; its data dictionary equals the live constants.
Crystal: the same image's PLL setting is the one that derives 84 MHz from an 8 MHz oscillator (PLL M = 4).
A working community mainline configuration for this printer selects STM32F401, FLASH_START_8000, CLOCK_REF_8M, USART1, 500000.
Upstream Klipper board_defs.py maps qidi-plus4 to the qidi-x7 definition (spi2, PB12, qd_mcu.bin / qd_mcu.CUR), and src/stm32/Kconfig maps STM32_FLASH_START_8000 to 0x8008000.
open_questions: A direct read of the stock board's SCB->VTOR is still missing (confirm 0x08008000 read-only, klippy stopped, before the first flash).
The HSE frequency is inferred (8 MHz); a mismatch would bring the board up at the wrong baud rate (recoverable through the SD bootloader).

toolhead.mcu_note: The chip may be a GD32F103 clone; Klipper builds it as stm32f103xe. Whether to set 'Disable SWD at startup' (STM32F103GD_DISABLE_SWD) is undecided.
toolhead.clock_ref: 8 MHz external crystal (STM32_CLOCK_REF_8M). HSE is certain (72 MHz is unreachable from the internal oscillator on an F1); 8 MHz is likely.
toolhead.bootloader: UNSETTLED. Either Katapult at 0x08000000 (a community add-on installed over SWD with an ST-Link) or the unknown stock bootloader.
toolhead.bootloader_baud: Katapult's baud rate is compile-time: 250000 (FreeDi) or 500000 (other community builds). Probe both. Unknown for a stock bootloader.
toolhead.method: Katapult flashtool over /dev/ttyS2, only if Katapult is detected by a read-only handshake at 250000 and 500000. If it is not detected, refuse: a first-time Katapult install needs an ST-Link, which Eitri cannot do. Never erase or overwrite a bootloader.
evidence: Live klippy.log of the printer: MCU=stm32f103xe CLOCK_FREQ=72000000 RESERVE_PINS_serial=PB7,PB6 SERIAL_BAUD=500000.

A community Plus 4 toolhead Klipper image is linked at 0x08002000 (reset handler position, and a vector table beginning with a RAM-top stack pointer 0x20005000), consistent with Katapult's 8 KiB layout. It says nothing about the factory layout.
That image's clock setting is PLL x9, which gives 72 MHz from an 8 MHz crystal.
A Q2 toolhead image suggests 0x08008000 for a stock layout, but it was never observed on a Plus 4.
open_questions: Does this printer's toolhead currently run Katapult or the stock factory bootloader? Check read-only: a Katapult handshake on /dev/ttyS2 at 250000 and 500000 (no write), and/or a debug_read of SCB->VTOR (0xE000ED08) and the words at 0x08000000/04 through klippy with klippy stopped. Needs permission to touch the printer.

Application offset from VTOR: 0x2000 means the Katapult-era layout, 0x8000 a stock Makerbase layout, anything else needs a new analysis. If stock, find the bootloader's flash protocol for ttyS2; nothing shows that hid-flash works on the toolhead.
Whether a QIDI OTA image exists that would settle both offsets directly (needs permission to contact QIDI servers).
Chip genuineness (GD32 clone) and the 'Disable SWD at startup' option must be settled before the toolhead build config is frozen.

conflicts: Toolhead flash offset: 0x08008000 (inferred from the Q2 sibling) versus 0x08002000 (Katapult 8 KiB). The sources assume different bootloader states.
Toolhead bootloader type: unknown, possibly a Makerbase UART bootloader, versus Katapult after an ST-Link install. Nothing shows what this printer runs.
Katapult baud: 250000 versus 500000 (compile-time). Only relevant if Katapult is present.
The old installer registry listed 'stm32f4*' as the toolhead chip and Katapult at 250000 for both boards; both were wrong and are fixed.
